key_insight: Quantum embedding captures molecular behavior in finite or crystalline environments while keeping active-subsystem calculations near gas-phase cost.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables efficient simulations of adsorption, solvent effects, and light-driven molecular dynamics without repeatedly computing the full surrounding material.
method: Compute the frozen host once and represent it using Gaussian-fitted electron density and nuclear charges.
Separate periodic electrostatics into explicit near-field and fast-multipole far-field contributions.
Use analytic gradients to relax the active subsystem and remove host atoms to create voids without supercells.
evidence_signal: Reported benchmarks include CO/MgO interaction energies within 0.44 kJ/mol of periodic DFT at 27× lower cost and a solvent shift within 0.01 eV of supermolecular CC2 at over 500× lower cost.
watch_item: The frozen-host approximation warrants validation when guest-induced polarization or structural changes in the environment are important.
paper_title: Quantum Embedding from Molecular to Crystalline Environments at the Cost of a Gas-Phase Calculation
